section_summary.extract_value: This section describes a single study investigating the relationship between body dissatisfaction and positive body image, focusing on the role of BMI and an affect regulation approach. The study found that BMI was a significant negative predictor of positive body image, and a perceived discrepancy between current and ideal body size was a consistent contributor to body dissatisfaction. The sample primarily consisted of heavier Black older adolescent females preparing to start college, and the findings highlight the importance of multicultural sensitivity in college health promotion.
